Comparing Strings & Naming Variables

The one idea to landEvery character is stored as a number (ord gives it, chr goes back), so Python compares strings by those numbers, one pair of letters at a time, and the first different pair decides. A variable name uses only letters, digits and _, never starts with a digit, is never a keyword, and in Python is written in snake_case.

Worksheet task 3: does Python accept this name?

Valid or not, and whyworksheet task 3

Worksheet · Task 3

Does Python accept this name?

User_namein(yes no)?1_age_player_agetotal.billWhileravi_kumar2

Python accepts

User_nameLetters and an underscore. It begins with a letter.
_player_ageIt may begin with an underscore.
WhileCapital W. Python keywords are small, so While is not one.
ravi_kumar2Digits are fine after the first letter.

Python refuses

inRule 4: in is a keyword. Python keeps it for itself.
(yes no)?Rule 2: a space, brackets and ? are not allowed.
1_ageRule 3: it begins with a digit.
total.billRule 2: a dot is a special character. Instagram allows it, Python does not.

Exit: one question

Exit: one question

Exit question

Which name gets no hall?

The exam cell sends each student to a hall by name. One student gets no hall at all.

halls.py
1name = input()2if name >= "A" and name < "N":3    print("Hall 1")4elif name >= "N" and name <= "Z":5    print("Hall 2")

Which name prints nothing at all?

  • name = "Arun"A is 65 and N is 78. "Arun" is less than "N", so it prints Hall 1.
  • name = "N""N" >= "N" is True, so it prints Hall 2. Equal counts for >=.
  • name = "Nandu""Nandu" starts with N, then has more letters, so it is bigger than "N" and smaller than "Z". Hall 2.
  • name = "Zoya"Z = Z, then "Z" runs out. The shorter one is smaller, so "Zoya" > "Z". Both conditions are False. Nothing prints.
📌

Key takeaways

Key takeaways: six examples

Key takeaways

Comparing strings and naming variables, in six examples

1

A letter is a number

print(ord("A"))

65

ord() gives the number. Capitals run 65 to 90.

2

A number is a letter

print(chr(97))

a

chr() goes the other way. Small letters run 97 to 122.

3

Small beats capital

print("a" > "A")

True

97 is more than 65. It is not the alphabet.

4

First different letter

print("BAT" > "BALL")

True

B = B, A = A, then T (84) beats L (76). Length does not count.

5

One runs out

print("98" < "984")

True

9 = 9, 8 = 8, then "98" has nothing left. Shorter is smaller.

6

A good name

total_bill = 90

Python accepts it

Letters, digits and _ only. No digit first. No keyword. snake_case.
